items.title: Film room: What Memphis did to overcome first half struggles to beat East Carolina
items.summary: Memphis football picked up a thrilling 41-34 overtime win over East Carolina to move to 6-2 on the season. Despite the win, the Tigers struggled offensively in the first half. Marcus Stokes and company scored just three points and could not find any success running the football.

items.title: "I knew it was going to him": Ellis Ellis Jr. on his game-ending interception
items.summary: Memphis' Ellis Ellis Jr. said he locked eyes with the receiver and knew where the ball was going before Mitch Griffis ever threw it. Moments later, he had the interception that secured the Tigers 41-34 overtime win over East Carolina.

items.title: Tigers Take Down East Carolina 41-34 in Overtime, Become Bowl Eligible for 13th Straight Season
items.summary: MEMPHIS, Tenn. – The University of Memphis (6-2, 3-1 American) football team overcame a two-score deficit in the second half, eventually defeating East Carolina (3-4, 1-2 American) 41-34 in overtime Thursday night in Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium.

items.title: Marcus Stokes' strong second half and more Memphis winners and losers from win over East Carolina
items.summary: Marcus Stokes and the Tigers came out firing in the second half with Hayes' long touchdown. Despite the drops, Memphis' air attack was very effective against a zone-heavy East Carolina defense.
